ENGLISH_ONLY: Write all internal research prose, fields, and messages in English. Preserve mathematical notation.

You are one persistent GPT-6 Pro research leaf. Perform exactly one round of the exact task your Extra High parent assigned to this node and round. Use the supplied durable research state when earlier conversation context is missing. State assumptions, pursue a proof, counterexample, or rigorous partial result, and distinguish evidence from conjecture. An unsuccessful attempt must still produce a report.

Return one JSON object matching OUTPUT_SCHEMA_JSON, inside a single fenced JSON code block with no surrounding text, so the web renderer preserves literal JSON strings. Copy node_id and round_id exactly from CONTEXT_JSON. Include status (SOLVED, PARTIAL, or STUCK), summary, findings, evidence, obstacles, recommended_next_steps, split_suggestion, and important_update. Include rigorous mathematical details in evidence; do not claim independent verification merely because you produced a proof. Use empty lists when appropriate. A split_suggestion only proposes tasks; it cannot create children or change the tree.

This report is mandatory even when stuck, interrupted by a mathematical obstacle, or solved. The scheduler stores it and delivers it to your parent, with human review if enabled. Stop after this one report. Your parent must assess it and create a complete new prompt before you may research again. Never select or start your own next round, never treat human discussion as approval, and never bypass the stored prompt/report approval gates.

{"goal": "Elementary finite-sum and trigonometric-correlation verification: seek a genuinely independent proof of the sharp cyclic inequality, validate equality and constants by exact finite calculations, and audit exceptional cases without disguising spectral arguments as elementary independence.", "kind": "leaf", "node_id": "n-3790f8503746", "research_state": "{\"evidence\": \"Write \λ\₂=4sin\²\θ and \γ=\λ\₂\−\λ\₁=\λ\₁(1+2cos\θ)>0 for N\≥4. All cyclic indices are modulo N; every norm is the unnormalized Euclidean norm.\ \ PROJECTION. The finite identity (1\−q)\∑_{j=0}^{N\−1}q\ʲ=1\−q\ᴺ gives \∑e^{ik\θj}=0 whenever N does not divide k. Consequently cosine and sine at frequency \θ have zero means, squared norms N/2, and inner product zero. Thus v=P_Nx has v_j=a cos(\θj)+b sin(\θj), where a=(2/N)\∑_l x_l cos(\θl) and b=(2/N)\∑_l x_l sin(\θl). Set z=x\−v. Then z is perpendicular to V_N, has zero mean, and M(x\−u)=M(z)+M(v\−u) for every u\∈V_N. Hence dist(x,V_N)\²=M(z). Cyclic summation by parts gives \∑\Δv_j \Δz_j=\∑(2v_j\−v_{j\−1}\−v_{j+1})z_j=\λ\₁\∑v_jz_j. The same recurrence gives E(v)=\λ\₁M(v), so expansion proves D(x)=D(z).\ \ REFLECTION REDUCTION. For each r=0,...,N\−1 set y_j=z_j\−z_{r\−j} and s_j=sin(\θ(j\−r/2)). Direct expansion gives \∑_r M(y)=2NM(z), \∑_r D(y)=2ND(z), and \∑_r y_j=Nz_j. Moreover, \∑_j y_js_j=2\∑_j z_js_j=0. At sine zeros, reflection fixes the vertex, so y_j=0. With t_j=y_j/s_j elsewhere and t_j=0 at these zeros, expansion using s_{j\−1}+s_{j+1}=2cos\θ s_j gives D(y)=\∑_j s_js_{j+1}(t_{j+1}\−t_j)\². A sign-changing edge has reflected endpoints: its intervening sine zero lies at its half-integer midpoint. Its ratios are therefore equal, so every negative-weight term vanishes.\ \ List the positive-sine vertices consecutively along a lifted cyclic arc. Their angles are h\₁,...,h_m\∈(0,\π), with spacing \θ. Put s_i=sin h_i, w_i=s_i\², a_i=s_i s_{i+1}, and retain t_i=y_i/s_i on this arc. Reflection duplicates its mass and positive-edge energy. Therefore, defining S=\∑_{i=1}^m w_it_i\² and T=\∑_{i=1}^{m\−1}a_i(t_{i+1}\−t_i)\², we have M(y)=2S, D(y)=2T, and \∑_{i=1}^m w_it_i=0. If m=1, the last identity forces y=0.\ \ NEW SHARP WEIGHTED CERTIFICATE. Assume m\≥2. Set \φ_i=cos h_i and p_i=a_i(\φ_i\−\φ_{i+1})>0 for 1\≤i<m, with p\₀=p_m=0. Sine addition proves\ p_i\−p_{i\−1}=\γw_i\φ_i, 1\≤i\≤m.\ Indeed, its left side equals s_i[(s_{i\−1}+s_{i+1})\φ_i\−s_{i\−1}\φ_{i\−1}\−s_{i+1}\φ_{i+1}], and the two relevant recurrences have factors 2cos\θ and 2cos(2\θ), respectively. At an omitted boundary edge, either the neighboring sine is zero, or the two angles are \±\θ/2 or \π\±\θ/2 and have equal cosines. Thus its flux really is zero, covering odd and even N without discarded boundary terms.\ \ Define F_i=\∑_{k=1}^i w_kt_k, so F\₀=F_m=0, and J=\∑_{i=1}^{m\−1}F_i\²/a_i. Since S=\∑_{i=1}^m(F_i\−F_{i\−1})\²/w_i, direct expansion yields the dual factorization\ K:=S\−\γJ=\∑_{i=1}^{m\−2}(p_ip_{i+1}/w_{i+1})(F_i/p_i\−F_{i+1}/p_{i+1})\²\≥0.\ To check every diagonal coefficient, use\ (p_i\−p_{i\−1})/w_i\−(p_{i+1}\−p_i)/w_{i+1}=\γp_i/a_i.\ The cross coefficients on both sides are \−2F_iF_{i+1}/w_{i+1}. Finally, finite summation by parts gives \∑_{i=1}^{m\−1}F_i(t_{i+1}\−t_i)=\−S. Expanding squares now proves the explicit strengthened certificate\ T\−\γS=\∑_{i=1}^{m\−1}a_i(t_{i+1}\−t_i+\γF_i/a_i)\²+\γK\≥0.\ Averaging over reflections gives D(z)\−\γM(z)=N\⁻\¹\∑_r(T_r\−\γS_r)\≥0, proving the requested estimate.\ \ COMPLETE EQUALITY. If T\−\γS=0, then K=0. Its positive coefficients force F_i=\κp_i; for m=2 this proportionality is automatic because there is only one coordinate. Hence t_i=(F_i\−F_{i\−1})/w_i=\κ\γ cos h_i. Reflection and the zero vertices show that y_j is proportional to sin(2\θ(j\−r/2)). The singleton case gives y=0 and satisfies the same conclusion. Equality after averaging forces this conclusion for every r. Since z_j=N\⁻\¹\∑_r y_j, it follows that z belongs to W_N=span_R{cos(2\θj),sin(2\θj)}. This excludes all additional equality cases.\ \ SHARPNESS AND SMALL N. For N\≥4, finite geometric sums at frequencies 1,2,3 show W_N is perpendicular to constants and V_N. For N\≥5, its cosine and sine have squared norms N/2 and inner product zero. At N=4, its sine vanishes and its cosine is (\−1)^j, with squared norm 4. For every w\∈W_N, the direct recurrence 2w_j\−w_{j\−1}\−w_{j+1}=\λ\₂w_j and summation by parts give E(w)=\λ\₂M(w), hence D(w)=\γM(w). A nonzero cosine therefore proves optimality, and stability equality is exactly x=v+w with v\∈V_N and w\∈W_N. Original Poincare equality instead requires w=0.\ \ For N=4, \γ=2 and the orthogonal spaces V_4 and W_4 have dimensions 2 and 1, exhausting the mean-zero space. Thus D(x)=2dist(x,V_4)\² for every admissible x; the alternating vector has M=4 and E=16. For N=5, \γ=\√5 and both harmonic spaces have dimension 2, exhausting the four-dimensional mean-zero space; therefore D(x)=\√5dist(x,V_5)\² identically. For N=3, V_3 already has dimension 2, equal to the mean-zero space. Direct expansion gives E=3M, so D=dist\²=0. Every stability coefficient then works vacuously; there is no meaningful finite optimal coefficient.\ \ NEAR EXTREMIZERS. For N\≥4, nonzero x, and \ε\≥0, E(x)/M(x)\≤\λ\₁+\ε implies dist(x,V_N)/||x||\₂\≤min{1,sqrt(\ε/\γ)}. For every 0\≤\ε\≤\γ, choose x=v+w with M(w)/(M(v)+M(w))=\ε/\γ; these mixtures attain equality. Thus the coefficient is optimal even for arbitrarily small \ε. For \ε>\γ, the untruncated bound exceeds 1, while the sharp truncated bound is attained by a nonzero second harmonic. The zero vector satisfies the homogeneous inequality but has no defined Rayleigh quotient. Equivalently, with C_N=1/\λ\₁,\ C_N E(x)\−M(x)\≥(1+2cos\θ)dist(x,V_N)\².\ Thus C_N E(x)/M(x)\≤1+\δ implies normalized distance at most min{1,sqrt(\δ/(1+2cos\θ))}.\ \ METHOD. The additional coercivity is proved by explicit finite-sum square expansions and boundary identities, not inferred from Round 1 nonnegativity. No harmonic-basis expansion, eigenvalue ordering, or spectral minimization is used.\", \"findings\": [\"Reflection averaging reduces the mean-zero cyclic inequality to inequalities for reflection-antisymmetric vectors.\", \"A directly expanded sine-weighted factorization proves positivity: every negatively weighted square vanishes by reflection symmetry.\", \"The equality space is exactly the real first-harmonic span.\", \"The exact averaged sum-of-squares certificate supplies an elementary starting point for future stability analysis.\", \"The elementary orthogonal projection onto V_N removes the first harmonic without changing D(x).\", \"An explicit second finite-sum factorization supplies the additional coercivity required beyond the Round 1 nonnegative certificate.\", \"For N>=4, the optimal coefficient is gamma_N=lambda_1(1+2cos(theta)), with stability equality exactly on the sum of the first- and second-harmonic subspaces.\", \"Stability is an identity throughout the mean-zero space for N=4 and N=5. For N=3, both the deficit and the distance vanish identically.\", \"The normalized near-extremizer bound is sharp, including for arbitrarily small positive deficits.\"], \"important_rounds\": [\"n-3790f8503746-r000001\", \"n-3790f8503746-r000002\"], \"last_round
